original_question: Consider the nonlinear Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem on a finite interval 0<x<L: u_t+u u_x+u_{xxx}=0, u(x,0)=phi(x), together with the boundary conditions u(0,t)=0, u(L,t)=0, and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t). Is this nonlinear problem well-posed in H^s(0,L) for any Sobolev index s?
target_in_paper: Section 4 open problem following Eq. (4.23) in the arXiv version of the paper (the same problem appears as Eq. (4.6) in the published journal version): whether the nonlinear KdV IBVP on (0,L) with u(0,t)=u(L,t)=0 and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t) is well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact nonlinear equation used in this open problem, the finite-interval setting 0<x<L, the initial datum u(x,0)=phi(x), the boundary conditions u(0,t)=0, u(L,t)=0, and u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t), and the fact that the issue is well-posedness in a Sobolev space H^s(0,L). It also correctly keeps the transport term u_x out of the equation; that omission is faithful here, because this particular open problem is posed for u_t+u u_x+u_xxx=0 rather than for the earlier general model with an added u_x term.
missing_details: The paper asks an existential question: whether the nonlinear IBVP is well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some Sobolev exponent s in R, not for every or any Sobolev index.
It should be made explicit that L>0 is fixed, x belongs to (0,L), t>0, and phi is the prescribed initial datum in H^s(0,L).
To be fully stand-alone, the differential operators should be identified explicitly: u_x = partial_x u and u_xxx = partial_x^3 u.
The nearby context matters: this problem is singled out precisely because the general boundary-value method developed earlier in the paper does not handle it.

The paper notes that the associated linear problem u_t+u_xxx=0 with the same boundary conditions is already known to be well-posed forward and backward in time; the unresolved issue is the nonlinear term u u_x.

The paper does not ask for a characterization of all admissible s, nor for global well-posedness here; the question is only whether there exists at least one Sobolev index s for which the nonlinear IBVP is well-posed.
refined_question:
Let L>0 be fixed, let u=u(x,t) be real-valued on (0,L) x (0,∞), and let phi in H^s(0,L). Consider the nonlinear Korteweg-de Vries initial-boundary value problem
u_t + u u_x + u_xxx = 0,  x in (0,L), t>0,
u(x,0)=phi(x),
u(0,t)=0,  u(L,t)=0,  u_x(0,t)=u_x(L,t),  t>0,
where u_x = partial_x u and u_xxx = partial_x^3 u. Does there exist some Sobolev exponent s in R for which this nonlinear IBVP is well-posed in H^s(0,L)?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the last well-posedness question in Section 4. The boundary conditions match exactly the second special boundary problem isolated there, not the paper’s earlier general nonhomogeneous problem. In the surrounding discussion, the authors first note that this boundary problem is one of the cases their general approach does not cover, then record conservation of the L^2 norm for this class of problems, then state that the associated linear problem is already well-posed forward and backward in time, and finally pose the unresolved nonlinear question in the form: is the nonlinear IBVP well-posed in H^s(0,L) for some s? The main correction needed to your draft is the quantifier: the paper asks for existence of some s, not well-posedness for arbitrary s.
